key_insight: Building rotation and reflection invariance into quantum neural networks can reduce overfitting and prevent orientation-based shortcut learning.
engineering_relevance: For image tasks with symmetry-preserving labels, invariant quantum models can improve generalization from small training sets and retain accuracy gains under realistic simulated noise.
method: Compare four eight-qubit models with identical encoding, circuit structure and parameter counts, and equivalent dynamical Lie algebras.
Evaluate invariant and non-invariant models on image labels unchanged by the dihedral group D4.
Test generalization, class-dependent corner-watermark shortcuts and resilience to a realistic noise model.
evidence_signal: Across four binary tasks, including MNIST, galaxies and red blood cells, invariant models trained on a few tens of images generalized better, while moving shortcut watermarks often reduced non-invariant models to chance accuracy.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to eight-qubit models and four binary tasks; benefits depend on the chosen symmetries preserving task labels.
paper_title: Invariance can prevent overfitting and shortcut learning in Quantum Neural Networks
